analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: Midterms delivered a Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress. Initial reaction was duration-positive and risk-off: 10Y UST yields fell about 7bp toward 4.90% before giving some back as equities recovered, and DXY fell harder to just below 101.50.

Mizuho reads the sweep as lower fiscal optionality for the rest of Trump's term, but warns against chasing the rates rally because Trump could shift to 'deal-making mode' and keep fiscal expansion alive. 4.90% is the key support level in 10Y yields.
The 4.90% support level conflicts with yesterday's strong JOLTS print and oil near $104/bbl, which are less constructive for duration.
Iran headlines remain mixed. Trump has played down immediate escalation, but Iran is far from a deal and Hormuz disruption risks remain.
Today's focus moves from politics to macro and supply. ISM services is the main data point, and the QRA (Treasury refunding announcement) is the one to watch, especially for the curve.

Mizuho expects coupon sizes unchanged in the QRA, with incremental funding needs pushed into bills. There is a tail risk (not the base case) of cuts to 20Y issuance. The 20Y point looks rich on the curve, so unchanged sizes could leave it vulnerable.
Mizuho says delaying coupon increases can work for now, but shortening the maturity profile is not a durable answer to the fiscal imbalance.

European government bonds take direction from the UST rally and softer risk backdrop, but oil near $104/bbl and an ECB uncomfortable with inflation should limit how far Bunds follow. 10Y Bund yields swung sharply on Iran headlines yesterday and finished about 3bp higher.

Today brings October Eurozone CPI and an updated ECB wage tracker. Markets price a high probability of another ECB hike in December plus another 25bp in H1-27. Softer wages/CPI would give duration room to follow USTs, while sticky inflation keeps Mizuho cautious on the front end.

Gilts: 10Y yields rose to 5.25% yesterday, underperforming Bunds. A 25bp BoE hike on Thursday is effectively priced, so the debate is the path beyond it. Markets price considerably more tightening than economists do.

Asia: equities were mixed after a rough start on the midterm news. JGBs bear-steepened after a weak Rinban round instead of following USTs. USD/JPY fell sharply to test 157.50 before retracing above 158.
